prompt: A customer disputes a denial. The support team needs a plain-language explanation; an auditor needs evidence of the governing rule; an engineer needs to reproduce the model route. Which logging design supports all three without storing raw sensitive prompts indefinitely?

options.text: Store every raw prompt and response forever, then let each audience search the transcript.
Use governed decision traces with audience-specific views.
Store only the final denial label because one outcome should answer every question.
Store aggregate daily counts and ask the customer to resubmit the original case for investigation.

feedback.reason: Different audiences need different evidence; a minimized structured trace supports reconstruction while data minimization and retention controls limit exposure.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Evidence should record the decision inputs and versions needed for the purpose, with access and retention matched to obligations.
details.scenarioApplication: Different audiences need different evidence; a minimized structured trace supports reconstruction while data minimization and retention controls limit exposure.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A trace may still contain sensitive information; classify fields and define retention, deletion, and access controls.
details.errorCorrection: Check whether the record proves the actual decision or completed control, rather than only describing intended behavior.
details.transfer: Design the record around who needs to explain, audit, and debug each decision.

messages.text: Indefinite raw storage and unrestricted transcript search ignore minimization, retention, and audience access needs.
A final label omits the governing rule, relevant evidence, and route needed to explain or reconstruct the denial.
Daily counts cannot recover the inputs and versions used for this particular decision; resubmission may use changed evidence.

prompt: The legal team asks why a particular customer was denied, while model developers need to locate a drift source. The current dashboard reports only a weekly denial rate. What should the architecture add?

options.text: A second weekly chart by provider, with no per-decision identifiers.
A permanent full-conversation archive accessible to every analyst.
Add governed per-decision evidence and version links.
A model-generated explanation stored as the sole evidence of why the decision occurred.

feedback.reason: Aggregates identify trends but cannot reconstruct a specific decision; a generated explanation alone may not reflect actual evidence or control execution.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A trace should connect the actual inputs, decisions, and versions needed to investigate, and be governed for its intended audiences.
details.scenarioApplication: Aggregates identify trends but cannot reconstruct a specific decision; a generated explanation alone may not reflect actual evidence or control execution.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Minimize sensitive content and avoid representing a post-hoc narrative as proof of execution.
details.errorCorrection: Check whether the record proves the actual decision or completed control, rather than only describing intended behavior.
details.transfer: Separate trend monitoring from case-level explanation and technical reproduction.

messages.text: Another aggregate chart still cannot identify the inputs or route for the disputed decision.
Broad permanent access increases exposure and does not define the evidence needed for each purpose.
A later narrative can be plausible yet inconsistent with the actual evidence and executed controls.

course.title: Responsible AI, Safety & Risk, Architect Module 3

prompt: An auditor needs evidence that every case requiring high-risk review received it during a defined period. Engineers also need to identify the threshold that triggered each route. Which evidence most directly supports both checks?

options.text: A monthly percentage of cases routed, with no case or reviewer references.
A prompt that says high-risk cases should receive review.
A dashboard screenshot captured after the audit request.
Reconcile required cases with reviews and trigger versions.

feedback.reason: Reconcile the complete set of cases requiring review against per-case completion events, including trigger/rule version, reviewer identity or role, disposition, and timestamps. Investigate missing matches.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A completed event demonstrates one review; population reconciliation is needed to support a claim that every required review occurred.
details.scenarioApplication: Reconcile the complete set of cases requiring review against per-case completion events, including trigger/rule version, reviewer identity or role, disposition, and timestamps. Investigate missing matches.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Protect reviewer identity and sensitive case facts; validate log coverage and event provenance rather than assuming immutability proves completeness.
details.errorCorrection: Check whether the record proves the actual decision or completed control, rather than only describing intended behavior.
details.transfer: Make auditability observable in the workflow rather than inferred from configured intent.

messages.text: A routing percentage does not prove review completion for each required case.
A prompt expresses intent; it is not evidence that a human completed a review.
A dashboard screenshot without linked completion records cannot demonstrate coverage of the required case population.

course.title: Responsible AI, Safety & Risk, Architect Module 3

prompt: A user asks for a concise explanation of a document-based recommendation. The support team needs no access to another customer’s data, but engineers need enough trace data to reproduce retrieval. How should the system serve both?

options.text: Give a grounded explanation; restrict the technical trace.
Expose the complete engineering trace to every user so the explanation is transparent.
Return a generic “model decision” message and discard retrieval references to minimize logging.
Let the model invent a likely rationale from the final answer without recording retrieval evidence.

feedback.reason: Audience-specific explanations can be concise while the protected engineering trace keeps the provenance necessary for authorized reconstruction.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Explainability, audit evidence, and debugging traces are related but not identical artifacts.
details.scenarioApplication: Audience-specific explanations can be concise while the protected engineering trace keeps the provenance necessary for authorized reconstruction.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Document-level metadata may itself be sensitive; apply tenant access and retention controls to the trace.
details.errorCorrection: Check whether the record proves the actual decision or completed control, rather than only describing intended behavior.
details.transfer: Tailor the explanation to the user and preserve the minimum controlled evidence for technical diagnosis.

messages.text: The engineering trace can contain sensitive data that the user is not authorized to see.
A generic label and discarded references prevent both an actionable explanation and historical retrieval investigation.
An invented rationale is not grounded evidence of why the original recommendation occurred.

course.title: Responsible AI, Safety & Risk, Architect Module 3

prompt: A decision trace records a retrieved page URL, but that page has since been overwritten. The original excerpt and document version were not retained anywhere. An engineer must explain which evidence the assistant saw last month. What can the team honestly conclude?

options.text: Today’s page proves the exact content retrieved last month.
The URL alone guarantees historical content reconstruction.
Report the gap; capture governed versions for future use.
Ask the model to recall the old page and treat its answer as proof.

feedback.reason: A mutable URL identifies a location, not the bytes originally retrieved. Report the historical gap and retain governed versioned evidence or a resolvable immutable reference for future decisions.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A mutable URL identifies a location, not the bytes originally retrieved. Report the historical gap and retain governed versioned evidence or a resolvable immutable reference for future decisions.
details.scenarioApplication: A mutable URL identifies a location, not the bytes originally retrieved. Report the historical gap and retain governed versioned evidence or a resolvable immutable reference for future decisions.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Version capture must respect minimization, access, and retention requirements; do not promise indefinite raw storage.
details.errorCorrection: Separate recorded historical evidence from a current document, generated narrative, or replay.
details.transfer: Preserve governed evidence sufficient for the specific explanation or reconstruction claim.

messages.text: The page changed; its current content does not establish the original retrieved excerpt.
A URL can point to different content over time and does not itself preserve a version.
A generated recollection is not evidence of the actual retrieval result.

prompt: A user challenges a recommendation. A trace contains the actual relevant input facts, retrieved evidence, rule version, and final decision. A model-generated explanation cites a criterion absent from that record. What should support provide?

options.text: The generated criterion, because fluent explanations are authoritative.
Use recorded facts; flag the unsupported criterion.
The full private trace, including unrelated third-party information.
A guarantee that the model’s hidden reasoning matches its explanation.

feedback.reason: Explain the recorded decision using relevant facts and evidence, and flag the unsupported generated criterion. A plausible narrative does not prove the original decision process.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Explain the recorded decision using relevant facts and evidence, and flag the unsupported generated criterion. A plausible narrative does not prove the original decision process.
details.scenarioApplication: Explain the recorded decision using relevant facts and evidence, and flag the unsupported generated criterion. A plausible narrative does not prove the original decision process.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If recorded facts do not justify the decision, escalate for review rather than inventing missing evidence.
details.errorCorrection: Separate recorded historical evidence from a current document, generated narrative, or replay.
details.transfer: Preserve governed evidence sufficient for the specific explanation or reconstruction claim.

messages.text: Fluency cannot establish that the criterion was used in the recorded decision.
Explanation does not authorize disclosure of unrelated people’s private information.
The trace and generated explanation do not establish access to or fidelity of hidden model reasoning.

prompt: A historical trace preserves exact inputs, retrieved context, prompt and model identifiers, output, and routing events. A replay with the same configuration generates different wording. Which conclusion is supported?

options.text: The original record must be false because wording differs.
Exact configuration guarantees identical model text on every replay.
Delete the old output and replace it with the replay result.
Keep the original trace; replay text may differ.

feedback.reason: The stored trace records the original observed output and route. A replay can help investigate behavior but does not guarantee identical generation or replace the original evidence.

details.mechanismOrProperty: The stored trace records the original observed output and route. A replay can help investigate behavior but does not guarantee identical generation or replace the original evidence.
details.scenarioApplication: The stored trace records the original observed output and route. A replay can help investigate behavior but does not guarantee identical generation or replace the original evidence.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Distinguish reconstruction of recorded facts from exact regeneration; unavailable model versions can further limit replay.
details.errorCorrection: Separate recorded historical evidence from a current document, generated narrative, or replay.
details.transfer: Preserve governed evidence sufficient for the specific explanation or reconstruction claim.

messages.text: Different generation does not by itself contradict a preserved observation of the original run.
Configuration identity alone does not establish deterministic model generation.
Replacing the original observation destroys the historical evidence needed to investigate the challenged decision.
